title: Beehave
cue: behavior trees for NPC and enemy AI
summary: Behavior trees for NPC and enemy AI, built from selector, sequence and decorator nodes with your own action and condition scripts and a shared blackboard.
useWhen: Enemies or NPCs choose what to do by priority, re-checked every tick: patrol, chase, attack, flee, and cooldowns that would become a tangle of if-statements or one large state machine script.
avoidWhen: An enemy has two or three simple behaviors, where a short match statement is easier to follow; or the logic is modes with explicit transitions, such as player movement, menus, or game flow, which godot-state-charts suits better.
